title: Farm Work in Four Seasons
paragraphs: Spring is for planting. Farmers plough the field, put in seeds, and water them.
Summer is for looking after. Weeds must be pulled, insects watched, and water kept in the field.
Autumn is for harvesting. Everyone works, including children and old people.
Winter is for repair. Tools are fixed, the house is cleaned, and plans are made for spring.

title: One Hen
paragraphs: We have one hen. She is brown and not very big, and she has a loud voice.
Every morning she lays an egg and then tells the whole neighbourhood about it.
She follows my grandmother everywhere. When my grandmother sits down, the hen sits next to her foot.
She gives us one egg a day. My grandmother says that is enough. One hen, one egg, every morning.

title: Smells on the Farm
paragraphs: A farm has many smells, and not all of them are nice.
There is the smell of wet earth after rain, which most people like.
There is the smell of hay in the store room, dry and sweet.
And there is the smell of the animals, which visitors notice and farmers do not. They live with it every day.

title: Our Weekend Plan
paragraphs: On Saturday morning we will go to the market and buy vegetables for the week.
At noon my father will cook, and I will wash the dishes after lunch.
On Sunday we will visit my grandmother. She lives on a small farm outside the city.
I will help her feed the chickens. Then we will come home before dark.

title: What I Learned This Term
paragraphs: This term I learned about rules, time, shopping, and farms.
The unit I liked best was about farms. I did not know that rice is moved from a small box to a water field.
I also learned to ask the price before I buy something. My mother says this is a useful skill.
Next term I want to read one English book. A short one, but a whole book.
